tasks.short: Book purchase and sales invoices, bank lines and memorials in AFAS Profit all day.

today.trigger: Invoices arrive in the AP mailbox, sales orders close, the Rabobank statement lands each morning.
steps: Open the invoice PDF from the shared Outlook mailbox
Look up supplier, cost centre and site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) in AFAS
Key the header, lines and VAT code into the AFAS purchase journal
Route for approval in the AFAS workflow
Import the Rabobank statement and book the unmatched lines
drudgery: Retyping invoice data that already exists in the PDF or UBL file
Switching between mailbox, PDF and AFAS screens
today.time_sinks: Staffing agency and transport invoices with many lines per site and week, and bank lines without a clear reference.

lenses.faster: Invoices come in as UBL via Peppol or are read by OCR and an LLM, and AFAS gets a prefilled booking; the bookkeeper checks instead of types.
lenses.autonomous: A new invoice in the mailbox triggers recognition, supplier match, coding proposal and approval routing without anyone opening it.
lenses.ambitious: Every invoice booked the day it arrives, so the month close starts on day one with a complete purchase ledger.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping staffing agency invoices; what remains is solving the odd ones and talking to suppliers.
lenses.options: For unclear invoices the system offers the two or three most likely bookings with the history behind each.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the booking rules, supplier master data and the exception queue, and tunes them monthly.
reach: Accountant: first-pass month-end accruals from booked-not-received data
Credit and Collections Officer: daily cash application on receivables

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which supplier, site manager or contract a strange invoice belongs to, and when something looks wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps across mailbox, recognition and AFAS with exceptions; a person approves postings that fall outside the rules.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice in the AP mailbox or Peppol inbox; daily bank statement import.
steps: Read UBL or OCR the PDF, extract header and lines
Match supplier, PO or agency order and propose GL, cost centre and VAT code
Post straight through when confidence and amount are within the rules
Queue the rest for the bookkeeper with the reason
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every exception and any invoice above an agreed amount before it posts.
data_needed: 12 months of posted invoices with coding
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history plus an exception log in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Dutch suppliers can send e-invoices in UBL over the Peppol network, which removes keying.
AFAS Profit supports digital invoice recognition and approval workflows.
LLM-based invoice extraction and coding proposals reach high straight-through rates on repeat suppliers.

risks: Wrong VAT code posted straight through causes BTW return errors
Duplicate payment when the same invoice arrives as PDF and UBL
Model drift when suppliers change invoice layouts
research_questions: What share of current invoice volume could arrive as UBL via Peppol within a year?
Which AFAS Profit module or partner does invoice recognition today, and at what accuracy on our suppliers?
How many invoices per month are staffing agency invoices, and can they match to portal hours automatically?

tasks.short: Check bookings and invoices for right amounts, VAT, cost centres and GL codes.

today.trigger: Before approving a booking batch, before a payment run and at month end.
steps: Pull the batch or journal listing from AFAS
Tick totals and VAT against the source documents
Check GL and cost centre codes against the coding list
Correct errors and ask colleagues about unclear lines
drudgery: Line-by-line ticking of correct entries to find the few wrong ones
today.time_sinks: Month-end checks of the whole period when errors are found late.

lenses.faster: Rule checks run on every posting and an LLM compares the posting to the source document, so the person only reviews flagged lines.
lenses.autonomous: Each night the checks run on the AFAS extract and produce an exception list before the team starts.
lenses.ambitious: 100 percent of postings checked instead of samples, which cuts audit adjustments at year end.
lenses.joy: No more ticking correct lines; the work becomes investigating the real anomalies.
lenses.options: Each flag comes with likely causes and a suggested correction.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the rule set and decides which checks matter for the auditor.
reach: Controller: continuous control testing evidence for the auditor
Accountant: pre-close review of the trial balance

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether an odd posting is an error, a one-off or a sign of fraud.
tasks.pattern_why: Most checks (sums, VAT rates, valid code combinations, duplicates) are writable rules on structured AFAS data; an LLM step only for document comparison.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly after the AFAS extract refresh, and before each payment run.
steps: Run rules: totals, VAT rate per GL, valid cost centre per site, duplicates
Compare posted amounts to the invoice document for a risk-based sample
Publish an exception list with reasons
Bookkeeper corrects or closes each exception
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper decides every correction; nothing is reversed automatically.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and valid code combinations
in_practice.logs_to: Exception register in SharePoint, linked to AFAS booking numbers

evidence.claim: Rule-based checks on ledger extracts can be built in Power BI or Python on a nightly data refresh.
Power BI is already refreshed nightly on an AFAS extract at the company.

risks: Too many false flags and people stop reading the list
Rules not updated when the chart of accounts changes
research_questions: What were last year's audit adjustments and which rule would have caught each?
How many postings per month are wrong today, and which kinds?
Does the AFAS extract include all fields needed (VAT code, cost centre, document link)?

tasks.short: Give invoices and documents the right GL, cost centre, site and VAT codes per our coding guide.

today.trigger: Each incoming invoice or expense document before booking.
steps: Read what was bought and for which site
Look up the coding guide in SharePoint or ask a colleague
Pick GL, cost centre, project and VAT code
Note the coding on the document or in AFAS
drudgery: Looking up the same codes for the same suppliers again
Chasing site managers about which site a cost belongs to
today.time_sinks: Mixed invoices covering several sites, and new suppliers without coding history.

lenses.faster: Coding is proposed from supplier history and invoice text; the bookkeeper accepts or corrects.
lenses.autonomous: Repeat suppliers with stable coding post without a human look.
lenses.ambitious: Consistent coding across three sites makes cost per site and per customer reliable for FP&A.
lenses.joy: Less lookup and chasing; more time for the new and unusual items.
lenses.options: Top three codings with confidence for each unclear invoice.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper curates the coding guide and approves new coding rules learned from corrections.
reach: FP&A Analyst: clean cost allocation per site for forecasts

tasks.human_edge: Knowing how a cost actually relates to operations, for example which warehouse a forklift repair belongs to.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured invoice text to a structured code set, checked by valid-combination rules inside the booking workflow.

steps: LLM reads lines and proposes GL, cost centre, site and VAT code
Rules check the combination is valid
High-confidence repeat cases pass; others go to the queue
Corrections feed back into the supplier coding history
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves codings below the confidence threshold and all new suppliers.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS booking with proposal and override recorded

evidence.claim: Classification of invoice lines to GL codes with an LLM using historical examples is feasible.

risks: Silent miscoding that shifts costs between sites
Coding guide out of date so the model learns old habits
research_questions: How often is coding corrected later, by whom and why?
What share of invoices come from suppliers with stable coding history?
Is the coding guide in SharePoint current and complete?

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, payment discounts, late interest and open balances per customer and supplier.

today.trigger: Payment runs, customer questions, overdue accounts and month end.
steps: Pull open items from AFAS
Calculate discount or statutory late interest in Excel
Check against contract terms
Book or communicate the result
drudgery: Rebuilding the same Excel calculation for each case
today.time_sinks: Disputed balances with partial payments and credit notes.

lenses.faster: Discounts, interest (wettelijke handelsrente) and balances are calculated by fixed formulas on AFAS data.
lenses.autonomous: Calculations run on every open item daily and show in the AR and AP overviews.
lenses.ambitious: Every early-payment discount taken and every late-interest claim considered, instead of the ones someone noticed.
lenses.joy: No more one-off spreadsheets; the left-over work is deciding whether to charge interest to a good customer.
lenses.options: Scenarios for paying early versus late per supplier given cash position.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the payment term and interest rules and checks the output.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: interest and dunning cost calculations
FP&A Analyst: cash forecast inputs from due dates

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether to actually claim interest or discount given the customer relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Formulas and terms are fixed and data is structured; no model needed to run it.

steps: Apply payment terms and discount rules per supplier and customer
Calculate statutory late interest on overdue items
Show amounts in AR and AP views
Flag cases where a claim or discount decision is needed
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper or Credit and Collections Officer approves any interest claim sent to a customer.
in_practice.logs_to: Calculation table in Power BI dataset, decisions in AFAS notes

evidence.claim: Dutch statutory commercial interest is a published rate set twice yearly, so it can be coded as a rule.
Microsoft Copilot in Excel can build and explain such formulas.

risks: Contract terms not captured in AFAS lead to wrong calculations
Claiming interest damages key customer relations
research_questions: Are payment terms for all customers and suppliers stored in AFAS, or only in contracts?
How much early-payment discount was missed last year?
How often is statutory interest claimed today?

tasks.short: Prepare payments for taxes, utilities and suppliers and build the Rabobank payment batch.

today.trigger: Weekly payment run, and tax deadlines for BTW and loonheffing.
steps: Select due invoices and tax assessments in AFAS
Check amounts, IBANs and payment references (betalingskenmerk)
Create the SEPA batch and upload to Rabobank
Get the second signature from the Controller or Finance Director
drudgery: Checking IBANs and betalingskenmerken by hand
Rebuilding the cash overview before each run
today.time_sinks: Last-minute urgent payments and changed supplier bank details.

lenses.faster: The run proposal is generated from due dates, approvals and cash, with IBAN and reference checks done by software.
lenses.autonomous: A draft batch is ready every payment day; tax payments are scheduled from the assessment date.
lenses.ambitious: Payments timed to maximise discounts and cash without missing a single tax deadline.
lenses.joy: No more manual IBAN checks; focus on the decisions about what to hold or pay early.
lenses.options: Two or three run scenarios: pay all due, take all discounts, protect cash at a set level.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper designs payment rules and bank-detail change controls rather than assembling batches.
reach: Controller: cash position reporting
FP&A Analyst: short-term cash forecast

tasks.human_edge: Accountability for money leaving the bank and spotting payment fraud such as fake IBAN change requests.
tasks.pattern_why: Multi-step with exceptions and real money; four-eyes approval in Rabobank must stay.

in_practice.trigger: Scheduled payment day or new tax assessment in AFAS.
steps: Select approved, due items and tax payments
Check IBAN against verified master data and the betalingskenmerk format
Propose the batch with cash impact
Bookkeeper reviews, then Controller signs in Rabobank
in_practice.human_gate: Two people approve every batch in Rabobank; IBAN changes need call-back verification.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payment run history and Rabobank audit trail

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit generates SEPA payment files from open payables.
Rabobank supports SEPA batch upload with multi-signature approval.

risks: Invoice fraud with changed IBANs if checks are trusted blindly
Missed BTW or loonheffing deadline causes fines
research_questions: How many IBAN change requests come in per year and how are they verified?
How long does a payment run take today from selection to signature?
Are tax payment deadlines tracked in AFAS or in a personal calendar?

tasks.short: Reconcile AFAS ledgers with bank statements, agency statements and our own Excel lists.

today.trigger: Daily bank import and month-end reconciliations.
steps: Export ledger balances from AFAS
Open the bank, agency or Excel list
Match items one by one in Excel
Investigate and book differences
drudgery: Matching hundreds of lines by eye
today.time_sinks: Agency statements that do not match invoices and hours, and partial payments.

lenses.faster: Matching rules pair items by amount, reference and date; only the residue goes to a person.
lenses.autonomous: Reconciliation runs after each statement import and posts a status per account.
lenses.ambitious: All balance sheet accounts reconciled monthly with evidence, not only bank and AP.
lenses.joy: No eye-matching; the remaining work is explaining real differences.
lenses.options: For each unmatched item, likely matches ranked with reasons.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns matching rules and reconciliation sign-off.
reach: Accountant: balance sheet reconciliations at month end
Controller: reconciliation evidence for the auditor

tasks.human_edge: Explaining differences and deciding the correcting entry.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching on structured statement and ledger data is rule based; an LLM only for messy references.

in_practice.trigger: Bank statement (CAMT.053) import or agency statement download.
steps: Load statement and ledger items
Auto-match on amount, reference, date
Suggest matches for remaining items
Bookkeeper resolves and books differences
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper signs off each reconciliation and every correcting entry.
in_practice.logs_to: Reconciliation file per account per month in SharePoint

evidence.claim: Rabobank provides statements in CAMT.053/MT940 formats suitable for automatic matching.
AFAS Profit can match bank lines to open items automatically.

risks: Agency portal formats change without notice
research_questions: What is the current auto-match rate on bank lines in AFAS?
Which side spreadsheets exist and can they be retired?
Can the three agency portals export statements in a stable format?

tasks.short: Answer questions from colleagues, suppliers and customers about invoices, payments and balances.

today.trigger: Emails and Teams messages: 'has my invoice been paid?', 'what is our balance?', site manager budget questions.
steps: Read the question in Outlook or Teams
Look up the invoice, payment or account in AFAS
Check bank or approval status
Reply by mail or phone
drudgery: The same 'when will I be paid' question many times a week
Looking up status in several screens
today.time_sinks: Questions with unclear references and back-and-forth with suppliers.

lenses.faster: An assistant reads the mail, finds the invoice and status in AFAS and drafts the answer.
lenses.autonomous: Status questions from known suppliers get a drafted reply in the queue within minutes.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers get self-service answers on their spend and open invoices.
lenses.joy: Fewer repeat questions; more time for the questions that need thought.
lenses.options: Drafts in Dutch or English, short or detailed.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper defines which questions can be answered automatically and checks quality.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: customer balance queries
HR Administrator: questions about flex worker invoices

tasks.human_edge: Handling upset suppliers and sensitive questions, and judging what can be shared.
tasks.pattern_why: Answers go to external parties and depend on context; the person stays the sender.

in_practice.trigger: New mail in the AP or AR mailbox or a Teams question.
steps: Classify the question and extract invoice or account references
Look up status in AFAS
Draft reply with the facts
Bookkeeper reviews and sends
in_practice.logs_to: Outlook sent items and AFAS notes

evidence.claim: Reading AFAS data via its API connectors for a lookup assistant is feasible.

risks: Sharing data with the wrong party (AVG/GDPR, commercial confidentiality)
Wrong status given from stale data
research_questions: How many questions per week arrive and what share are payment status questions?
Can AFAS data be exposed safely to an assistant with role-based access?
Would a supplier portal remove most of these questions?

tasks.short: Watch open receivables, leases and loans so payments come in and go out on time.

today.trigger: Weekly ageing review and due dates on lease or loan schedules.
steps: Run ageing reports in AFAS
Compare to the lease and loan schedules in Excel
Flag overdue items to the Credit and Collections Officer
Check that scheduled instalments were paid
today.time_sinks: Customers with disputes mixed into the overdue list.

lenses.faster: Daily ageing and schedule checks run automatically and only overdue or missed items show.
lenses.autonomous: Alerts go out the day a payment is missed, with reminders drafted for routine cases.
lenses.ambitious: DSO watched per customer daily and risk flagged before an account goes bad.
lenses.joy: No more weekly report building; the person deals with the customers who need attention.
lenses.options: Suggested next step per overdue account: reminder, call, hold deliveries.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper sets alert thresholds and dunning rules with the Credit and Collections Officer.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: first-line reminders
FP&A Analyst: cash-in forecast

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the customer relationship and deciding when to escalate or hold deliveries.
tasks.pattern_why: Due dates, balances and schedules are structured; alerts and reminders follow written rules.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract and bank import.
steps: Compute ageing and match instalments to schedules
Raise alerts for overdue or missed payments
Draft standard reminders for routine overdue items
Route disputed or large items to a person
in_practice.human_gate: Credit and Collections Officer approves escalations and delivery holds.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI ageing dashboard and AFAS dunning history

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit includes a dunning (aanmaning) process for overdue receivables.
Power BI is already used for finance dashboards on the AFAS extract.

risks: Automatic reminders sent to customers in dispute
Lease and loan schedules kept outside AFAS go stale
research_questions: What is current DSO and how much is more than 60 days overdue?
Where are lease and loan schedules kept and who updates them?
How are disputes flagged today so they can be excluded from reminders?

role.altitude: From keying and checking bookings to running the AP/AR process: owning the booking and coding rules, supplier master data, matching rules and the exception queue, and reporting straight-through rates to the Controller.
reach: Accountant: month-end accruals and balance sheet reconciliations
Credit and Collections Officer: cash application and first-line reminders
Controller: control evidence and reconciliation files for the auditor
FP&A Analyst: cash-in and cash-out inputs for the forecast
HR Administrator: checking staffing agency invoices against approved flex hours
role.ceiling_note: Of the roughly 600 hours per FTE per year these eight tasks cover, about half can go. The limits are payment approval (four-eyes in Rabobank), fraud judgement, supplier and customer relations, and how clean the AFAS master data is. Peppol uptake among suppliers and the formats of the three agency portals set how far straight-through processing can get.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing booking, coding and matching rules
Exception analysis and root-cause fixing with suppliers
Power BI and data quality checks on the AFAS extract
Payment fraud awareness and bank-detail change controls
Prompt and review skills for AI-drafted replies, within AVG/GDPR limits
role.ambitious_version: With three people, Noordhaven runs AP/AR so most invoices book themselves on arrival, every posting is checked, all accounts reconcile daily and DSO is watched every day. That lets the month close in a few days with a forecast the business trusts, and frees the bookkeepers to check flex worker costs against agency hours for all three sites.
